candidates.name: Ramp of overlapping dyadic truncations for p>2 (with its error estimate I14)
candidates.statement: u = sum_{k<l} (v_{<=2^{k+l}} - v_{<=2^k}), i.e. u_e = m_l(|v_e|) v_e with multiplicities 1,2,...,l,...,2,1 on the dyadic magnitude bins. Energy b = p log2 (l^p + 2 sum_{j<l} j^p) ~ l^{p+1}, the same at every edge; projection error ||Pu - u||_p^p <= C_p H^{p-2}(l+1). With l = ceil(L H^{1-2/p}) the relative error is <= C H^gamma / l and log K = O((log n)^{1-2/p}). A single window (or a constant-height rectangle) has energy/error ~ w/H^{p-2}, which only gives log K ~ (log n)^{p-2}, subpolynomial only for 2<p<3.

neighbours.ref: Fejer / de la Vallee Poussin summability (classical Fourier analysis; e.g. Zygmund, Trigonometric Series, Ch. III; Katznelson Ch. I)
neighbours.relation: Exact formal analogue: with partial sums S_k in place of truncations v_{<=2^k}, sum_{k<l}(S_{k+l} - S_k) = l (V_{l,2l} - sigma_l), l times the de la Vallee Poussin mean minus the Fejer mean, whose multiplier is the same triangular/trapezoidal window. Purpose is the same in spirit: averaging many sharp cutoffs gives a Lipschitz window whose per-cut error does not accumulate coherently (bounded Lebesgue constant vs log n for a single cutoff).

neighbours.ref: Logarithmic cutoff across dyadic scales in capacity / Dirichlet-energy arguments (zero capacity of points in R^2, Nash-Williams-type recurrence criteria, potential-theoretic energy decompositions over dyadic scales, e.g. arXiv math/0404088 Lemma on dyadic energy representation)
neighbours.relation: Same optimization: a unit rise spread as equal steps over N dyadic scales costs N (1/N)^q instead of 1 in a q-energy that adds over scales. 094's ramp is the dual extremal (maximize sum m_j^p over a window of width 2l subject to sum |Delta m_j|^p = O(l)), i.e. a discrete p-Poincare/Hardy extremal, solved up to constants by the tent.

neighbours.ref: Multi-scale averaged / Lipschitz cutoffs in metric embeddings (Bourgain 1985 averaging over scales; Krauthgamer-Lee-Mendel-Naor 2005 measured descent; random-scale truncation in Lipschitz extension)
neighbours.relation: Sum over scales of truncated (Lipschitz) distance functions so that errors at different scales do not add coherently.

final.justification: Non-analytic (test 2) and load-bearing (test 3, ~48% of the core) but test 1 fails at mechanism level. The ramp is ell times the de la Vallee Poussin-minus-Fejer window, transplanted from partial sums to magnitude truncations, and its gain is the standard spread-a-cutoff-over-scales effect (capacity log-cutoff; discrete Poincare extremal). Under the strict rule (a known device imported from another field is transfer) and given an estimated pivot distance of 1, it is a skilful adaptation, not a jump. Its specific role here is genuinely uncited and unprecedented in searches: it improves the exponent from (log n)^{p-2} (subpolynomial only for 2<p<3) to (log n)^{1-2/p}. That is why it is the family's maximum and the first item to re-open: it would be F3 if a discoverability run promoted it.

provenance_flag.explanation: The essential O(log n) localization (C7/I05) is GGNS, arXiv:2605.24130 (submitted 2026-05-22), whose abstract states (search-rendered, direct fetch blocked): "The initial proofs were generated by OpenAI's ChatGPT 5.5 Pro; the authors have verified and rewritten them to enhance readability and provide additional context." GGNS contains I05 (same) and none of the graded candidates C1-C6 (absent, abstract-level evidence). 094 re-proves GGNS in App. A and in Lean, so correctness does not depend on it, but the full p-range does: with the human SRS18 O(log^2 n) bound the method gives only 3/2<p<4 (analyst's computation; the paper does not state this). The other model-produced citation, OpenAI2026DoublingHilbert (family 098), is background only. Naor-Ren 2026 (lower bound) shows no AI disclosure in the abstract renderings. 'partial' = the headline builds on an essential model-produced result, while the family's own candidate items have human (classical) neighbours, not model-produced ones. Open: whether GGNS's ChatGPT 5.5 Pro work and the 094 manuscript came from one OpenAI pipeline (GGNS precedes 094 by four months; nothing found either way).

bridge_novelty.import: Electrical networks / spectral graph theory (transfer-current localization, GGNS/SRS18) -> nonlinear metric dimension reduction in L_p (C3+C7)
bridge_novelty.evidence: No prior use of electrical-flow localization in metric embedding or dimension reduction was found; SRS18's stated applications are oblivious routing on transitive graphs and min-cost flow (arXiv:2111.10368), and a targeted search of GGNS applications found none outside graph algorithms. The link is natural in hindsight: V is the cut space of the complete graph with conductances 1/delta_e^2, and P is its transfer-current matrix. Per PLAN, a new bridge is recorded separately and is not a jump. Note that its key input is itself model-produced (GGNS).

bridge_novelty.import: Stable laws / Levy measures -> L_p dimension reduction (C2, I08-I11)
bridge_novelty.evidence: Indyk 2006; Schechtman 1987/2011; stable embeddings of l_p^m into L_p (BDK, LePage); all in L or classical.

bridge_novelty.import: Maurey empirical method + minimax -> coordinate sampling (C4)

bridge_novelty.evidence: Rosenthal 1970 is itself a paper on subspaces of L_p, p>2; Pinelis 2015.

bridge_novelty.import: Change of density / reweighting to upgrade average to uniform bounds (C3, Brouwer or minimax)
bridge_novelty.evidence: Lewis 1978 and Talagrand 1995 (in L) in the subspace-embedding problem; Raecke 2008 / Goranci et al. 2023 for electrical routings.

bridge_novelty.import: Fourier summability / capacity log-cutoff (tent profile over dyadic scales) -> truncation of a heavy-tailed vector field (C1)
bridge_novelty.status: new application of a known device (uncited by 094)
bridge_novelty.evidence: The ramp equals ell (de la Vallee Poussin - Fejer) with partial sums replaced by magnitude truncations; no prior use with truncations of stable/heavy-tailed variables found (searches in C1.test1).
Fixed-point existence of reweightings is standard (Lewis weights); the Lean removes it entirely in favour of convex separation.

common.models: Training cutoff strictly before 2026-05-22 (GGNS v1); this also clears Naor-Ren (2026-09), the 094 manuscript (2026-09-23), family 098 (2026-09-25) and the release (2026-10-06). Canary probes: the model must not know that n^{o(1)} dimension reduction in L_p has been claimed, the exponent gamma(p), or the GGNS 2 log n bound. No browsing or tools. Exclude the OpenAI lineage that produced 094 and GGNS (ChatGPT 5.5 Pro and successors); run it only as an uncontrolled reference arm. Proposer and judge must differ. Fejer/de la Vallee Poussin, capacity log-cutoffs, Lewis weights, Schechtman, Indyk and Eskenazis are old background every model has seen; that is the point of grading against them.
common.context_L_minus: Mathlib d13f23b digest (measure theory, Lp, convexity) plus the 094 bibliography minus GGNS and Naor-Ren, as abstracts plus invoked statements; the GGNS bound is given as a bare statement ('|| |Q| ||_{2->2} <= 2 log n') only in arms that need P.

arms.L: adds GGNS and Naor-Ren full abstracts, to measure their effect
arms.directed: states the architecture up to the hidden item and gives all non-hidden upstream items

common.sampling: n = 256 per arm at T = 1.0 with a fixed reasoning budget; unbiased pass@k for k in {1,2,4,...,256}; K = 256.
common.judging: Two independent LLM judges given 094's precedent remarks (paper.tex:170-204) and this neighbour list; a Banach-space/probability expert checks all hits and 10% of misses. Lean where possible: a proposed profile m can be substituted for dyadicRamp (DyadicRamps.lean:18) and tested against the statement of ramp_sum_bounded_law (RampSum.lean:12) / ramp_projection_error (RampError.lean:34).
common.controls: Positive: Cook-Reckhow ER variables (calibration across families). Negative: C4 (weighted criterion), I16 (global cut), I14 (dyadic interpolation), in the same format.
common.prompt_template: Problem: Fix p>2. Show every n-point subset of L_p embeds in l_p^d with distortion D>1 and d = n^{o(1)}. Library: [L- digest]. Established: [upstream items]. [directed arm: A random F in V with sup-norm K and lambda-weighted relative p-moment error eta suffices, with d ~ K^{2p}/(eta b)^2 log n. P is an l2(sigma)-contraction onto V with row sums <= H = O(log n); v_e(r,t) = r g_e(t) under the intensity p r^{-p-1} dr has identical magnitude law on every edge. Truncating v to one window (1,2^w] gives energy ~ w and projection error^p ~ H^{p-2}, hence only log K ~ (log n)^{p-2}.] Propose the single most useful new definition or construction, stated precisely, with a proof sketch.

P-C1.item: C1, the ramp of overlapping dyadic truncations (I13 + I14)
P-C1.hide: eq. above-ramp and everything downstream: eq. above-energy, above-basic-bounds, above-projection-error, above-relative-error, the choice l ~ H^gamma, Poisson sampling of Z, the global cut and the p>2 entries of the contract table; Lean DyadicRamps, RampLaws, RampError, RampRetraction, ProjectedRamps, RampSum, AboveParameters, AboveTwo.
P-C1.arm_A_pivot: directed arm, including the single-window computation (energy w vs error H^{p-2}); high hit rate expected (estimated pivot distance 1).
P-C1.arm_B_decisive: Do not state the single-window computation; give only the architecture, P, the homogeneous increments, and the goal 'a random gradient for p>2 with log K = o(log n)'.
P-C1.equivalence: Hit: any multiplier u_e = m(log2|v_e|) v_e (or equivalent combination of magnitude truncations) whose profile m has bounded increments per dyadic level and height comparable to its width (tent, trapezoid, sine-like or any Lipschitz-in-log-scale bump), with the claimed trade energy ~ w^{p+1} vs error^p ~ H^{p-2} w, giving log K = O((log n)^{c}) with c<1 for every p>2. Partial: a smooth or Lipschitz log-scale cutoff with the right intuition but the wrong bookkeeping. Miss: single truncation, uniform window, or a rescaling of one window.

P-C2.hide: Section 'Clipping and projection' (paper.tex:619-706) and the p<2 contract entries; Lean StableRetractions, ClippedMoments, GradientSampling.stable_gradient_weighted, BelowTwo.
P-C2.equivalence: Hit: project a clipped stable-like Y in V back with P and use the logarithmic growth of the capped p-th moment to make the additive O(H^{2-p}) error relatively small, with T = exp(Theta(H^{2-p})).

P-C3.hide: Lemma projection (paper.tex:410-463) and its Lean replacement (Retractions.lean, ConvexSelection.lean:160-236); give GGNS as a bare statement.
P-C3.equivalence: Hit: any choice of weights sigma >= c lambda making every row sum of the l2(sigma) projection onto V O(log n) (fixed point, minimax, multiplicative weights or Lewis-type), or a retraction with the same row-sum and energy bounds.
